references.text: Joshua receives the same promise that every place where they set their foot will belong to them, with the same geographical boundaries from the wilderness to Lebanon and from the Euphrates to the Mediterranean Sea.
Moses promises Caleb that the land he has walked on will belong to him and his descendants, confirming the principle that the land where one's foot treads will become theirs.
God's covenant with Abraham, in which He promises the land from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates, which is the same territory promised in Deuteronomy.
God sets Israel's boundaries from the Red Sea to the Philistine sea and from the wilderness to the river, matching the geographical limits mentioned in this text.
The description of the borders of the Promised Land that Moses was commanded to distribute among the children of Israel.
An earlier reference in Deuteronomy where God commands them to go in and take possession of the land He swore to give their fathers, including the area up to the Euphrates.
